I want to agenda the topic of AI in the EIP ecosystem. I think we do not have to discuss adding `AGENTS.md` to the ecosystem https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12661 but I am not yet convinced if we should auto-merge documents which pass CI and pass the checks AI could do. 

My general fear is that if we write EIP documents by AI and also review them by AI, then these root documents are all written by AI. We should move carefully here. From my perspective these documents are used to communicate ideas (specifications) with the community and also serving as an archive/memory to document why we did specific things. Documents written by AI are clean and convincing, but could not be what the author originally wanted. It is thus important that we as ecosystem as whole figure out what we as community want and collaborate with the authors to reach that point. If this is all done by AI, then the future concepts are not written by us, but only by AI, and this might not converge to the similar specification if we would only do this by humans. The world is moving fast and it is evident we should accelerate our process, but this should still lead to equal results (yet faster).

> it is evident we should accelerate our process

👏 👏 👏 👏 

EIP/ERC editors are a precious resource and should be used where they can add the most value.  The biggest lift is increasing the quality of EIPs/ERCs by ensuring consistency in information & formatting and getting out of the way of winners being chosen.

When a PR is created we should review with AI (either through a bot or editor driven AI review) and automagically assign numbers (with some spam prevention). Once a PR passes AI checks it should be automatically merged.  The process to get a PR merged should be quick and shouldn't be gated on humans.  Number assignment could happen on merge but only if the overall process is quick

EIP/ERC editors should not decide winners (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-5069#mission).  Having manual processes means editors are potentially getting in the way of winners being chosen.  I have assigned 758 numbers (since we moved to sequential numbers), 266 PRs are still open (for a variety of reasons)!

Alternative sites to https://eips.ethereum.org have been created, partly in response to the time it takes to get a PR merged.  e.g. https://eips.sh, https://eip.tools & https://forkcast.org/eips/

### ERCs

ERCs: developers decide via adoption which application layer standards are "winners". 
Attention matters for adoption and having a draft ERC (merged PR) reportedly helps with this. (which is why we see developers keen to get PRs merged).

I have assigned 454 numbers to ERCs (since we moved to sequential numbers), with 217 PRs still open (for a variety of reasons).  Our processes should be ensuring all draft ERCs that meet the bar for information & formatting get merged quickly and let application developers decide which win.  Whilst this will likely increase the number of ERCs it will get editors out of the way of developers deciding winners.  ERCs which don't get traction (and hence aren't updated or progressed beyond draft) should be automatically moved to stagnant.

### EIPs

EIPs: client teams via all core devs decide which EIPs get proposed, declined, considered & scheduled for inclusion ("winners").  

The EIP process should work for core devs (and not the other way around).  The best place to track EIPs is already Forkcast.  It includes unmerged PRs once numbers have been assigned, along with information around governance decisions.

Whilst auto merging will increase the number of draft EIPs.  The bottleneck will be the all core devs governance process, which is already straining and I expect to see more and more use of AI to decide which EIPs get to PFI/CFI and also that the bar (e.g. tests, implementations) gets higher.
